title: (No AI) Perplexity’s Personal Computer turns Windows PCs into AI agents
author: Jess Weatherbed
content:
![Vector collage of the Perplexity logo.](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/chorus/uploads/chorus_asset/file/25472503/STK271_PERPLEXITY_C.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0,0,100,100)

Perplexity has expanded its agentic Personal Computer tool to Windows, allowing computers running the world's most popular OS to be used as a locally run AI system. Like the [Mac version](https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence/893536/perplexitys-personal-computer-turns-your-spare-mac-into-an-ai-agent) that Perplexity launched in April, Personal Computer for Windows operates like a "general-purpose digital worker" that can access local files and apps to perform actions on your behalf, such as creating documents and updating spreadsheets.

This launch builds on Personal Computer integrations that Perplexity launched for [Microsoft's 365 workspace apps](https://www.perplexity.ai/hub/products/integrations/microsoft) and [Teams virtual meeting software](https://www.perplexity.ai/hub/blog/computer-in-teams-is-here) in May. Personal Computer for Windows aims to bridge the remaining gap by …

title: (No AI) Smart rings are looking like my kind of AI gadget
author: David Pierce
content:
![Image of a ring.](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2025/11/RING.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0,0,100,100)

Over the last few months, I've spent a lot of time talking to my computer. One underrated feature of the LLM revolution has been a remarkable leap in all kinds of dictation technology - even the fastest, cheapest models are getting very good at understanding and processing speech. I've tested lots of these apps, from WisprFlow to Monologue to Spokenly to Handy to so many others, and have found them all to be useful ways to quickly write emails, Slack messages, and more.
